name: SQLScript
title: SQLScript (SAP HANA 2.0 SPS 08)

type.text: **NULL is a member of every domain**: procedure parameters, locals, and table columns carry NULL unannounced, and no signature states whether a value may be absent
**No sum types**: an alternative is a nullable column or a table variable's shape, and the consumer re-derives the encoding from the body

**Statements state no effect**: the reference defines the functional extension as side-effect free by intent, but the signature of a procedure states nothing about the writes, reads, or calls inside it

**Foreign code rides in-process**: procedures and functions can be defined in R or other languages inside the server, and the boundary between SQLScript values and the embedded runtime is checked by neither side's compiler

construction.text: **Table variables are the unit**: the data extension defines table types without tables, and procedures pass and assign table variables the optimizer can treat as sets rather than rows

**The reference argues against its own imperative layer**: the motivation chapter sets one-tuple-at-a-time semantics against set-oriented SQL because loops are "hard to optimize and parallelize", so the procedural constructs carry a documented performance warning the declarative ones do not

memory.text: **Allocation is the engine's**: column store, delta merge, and statement memory live in the HANA process, and the SQLScript text allocates nothing

error.text: **The EXIT HANDLER decides, or the procedure dies**: handlers catch declared conditions and SQL error codes, and without one the error leaves the procedure — no value carries the failure
**No composable result type**: failures travel by exception and results by output table variables and result sets, and neither threads through an expression

concurrency.text: **Session state is shared**: session variables and temporary tables are visible across every procedure the connection calls, so two callers share what the session holds

platform.text: **The procedure runs only in HANA**: the parser, the table-type system, and the deployment model (HDI containers) are the engine's, and nothing in the language runs elsewhere
**A poor fit outside the data tier**: the language has no general libraries or error values, so application logic beyond data flows builds every abstraction itself

performance.text: **The optimizer is the point**: the reference's stated goal is pushdown with "massive parallelization", and declarative bodies (UNION ALL with implicit parallelism, MAP_MERGE-style operations) are the constructs the engine optimizes
**Imperative bodies carry a documented penalty**: the reference motivates SQLScript itself by the cost of row-wise logic, and the same warning applies to loops written inside the language

ecosystem.text: **A proprietary stack end to end**: the server, the deployment infrastructure, the IDE (Business Application Studio), and the support model are SAP products under commercial terms

evolution.text: **The SPS calendar governs the surface**: HANA 2.0 moves in support-package stacks, and the reference's own version selector decides which constructs a deployment's procedures may use

domain.text: **The language exists to serve SAP's data tier**: procedures deploy through HDI into containers, the calculation and SQL engines define what they can say, and the S/4HANA application world is the domain

learning.text: **Two styles, one language**: set-oriented SQL and imperative blocks share the surface, and the reference's own guidance on when each applies is required reading before a body will perform

syntax.text: **Standard-shaped, SAP-flavored**: the statements read like ISO SQL, and the table-type system, handler syntax, and deployment annotations are HANA's own layer on top

testing.text: **No standard test harness for user procedures**: SAP's own QA is internal, and the documented testing story is application-side tests and the SQL analyzer against a live system

security.text: **Dynamic SQL is string-built**: EXEC runs SQL text assembled at run time, so concatenated user input reaches the parser, and the mitigation is the privilege model plus bound inputs

reproducibility.text: **A procedure is deployed source**: the same HDI artifact on the same server version and data reproduces the same result, and nothing is compiled ahead of the call outside the deployment
**No toolchain pin exists in the artifact**: the repository names no server revision — the executing release is a deployment fact the HDI container records elsewhere

supplychain.text: **No signed provenance for published procedures or add-ons**: deployment artifacts move through SAP's channels under commercial terms, with no signature-checked public channel
**No advisory feed names the language surface**: security fixes land in SAP notes and support packages, with no public CVE-mapped advisory database for the engine's dependencies

observability.text: **No tracing standard is part of the language**: PlanViz, the SQL analyzer, and the trace configuration are server features, and the procedure text carries no trace hook
**No structured logging in the language**: messages leave through SIGNAL and the server log, and no logging construct exists in SQLScript

feedback.text: **The vendor's IDE completes the code**: SAP Business Application Studio publishes SQLScript tooling with code completion and the SQL analyzer beside it
**No procedure debugger ships in the standard toolchain**: diagnosis goes through the SQL analyzer, PlanViz, and handler instrumentation

interop.text: **No portable target**: the body compiles in one vendor's engine, and nothing in the language runs without a HANA server

governance.text: **Governance is SAP**: the release calendar, the roadmap, and the language's direction are one company's, and no independent body can change them
**No public specification exists**: the SQLScript Reference documents the implemented behavior of one product line, and no independent implementation follows from it
**Correctness is what HANA does**: no conformance suite exists for SQLScript, and the one implementation is the oracle

tradeoffs: **Pushdown is the design goal**: table types, set-oriented bodies, and in-engine parallelism exist to keep data from moving, and the price is that the imperative layer carries a documented optimization warning
**Deployment is the database**: HDI containers version procedures and table types as artifacts, and the price is that the application's logic lives inside a commercial engine's deployment model
**Handlers are optional**: EXIT HANDLER gives structured recovery against conditions and SQL error codes, and the price is that unhandled errors surface at the caller
**Embedded R and Python buy in-database analytics**: foreign-language procedures run beside SQLScript bodies, and the price is an unchecked boundary between two type systems
verdict: SQLScript is SAP HANA's collection of SQL extensions — table types without tables, side-effect-free functions, and imperative procedure bodies — deployed through HDI into the engine's containers. Its costs are the platform's own: NULL in every domain, failures that travel only by exception, session-wide state, a proprietary stack end to end, and a reference that documents row-wise constructs as the thing the optimizer exists to avoid. Main strengths: a stated design goal of pushdown and parallelism, table variables the engine treats as sets, in-database R and Python for analytics, vendor IDE tooling with the SQL analyzer, and one-volume reference documentation. Main weaknesses: no debugger or user-procedure test harness, no structured logging or tracing in the language, string-built dynamic SQL, single-vendor governance with no specification or conformance suite, and logic whose reproducibility rides a commercial engine revision the artifact does not name.

energy.text: Energy is the HANA process's: column store, delta merges, and the application's license bill pay, and the reader's levers are set-oriented body design the reference argues for.

ai-readiness.text: Generated procedures appear in SAP migration and extension work, and the traps are the layer the reference warns about: imperative bodies, handler scope, and dynamic SQL that no generated snippet prices.

safety.text: No certified path; the engine's transaction and recovery guarantees are SAP's, stated in its own documentation and support terms.

use:data.observation: procedures pass and assign table variables the optimizer can treat as sets

use:query.observation: set-oriented SQL and imperative blocks share the surface

delivery.target: deployed procedure and function source (HDI artifacts)
delivery.note: the database stores and parses the source at deployment and use; no compiled unit crosses a producer boundary
